newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Frei reshuffles cabinet before elections.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Frei reshuffles cabinet before elections.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei replaced top political adviser Genaro Arriagada and four other Cabinet ministers on Friday in a shakeup only a month before nationwide municipal elections.

Frei asked for the resignations of his entire cabinet and accepted those of Arriagada and the ministers of education, agriculture, planning, and transport and communications, said presidential spokesman Jose Joaquin Brunner.
"The rest of the resignations have been rejected," Brunner told reporters.
Local media had expected a reshuffle this week, partly to give a fresher image to Frei's centre-left coalition government before nationwide municipal elections on Oct. 27.
The elections are seen as a key political test for Frei, who took office for a six-year term in 1994, and the centre-left coalition government he leads.
Presidential Chief-of-Staff Arriagada will be replaced by Juan Villarzu, the president of state copper company Codelco and a prominent member of Frei's Christian Democratic party.
There was no official word on Arriagada's future but officials have said privately he was tipped to be the next ambassador to the United States.

Arriagada, Frei's top adviser and point man with Congress, came under criticism for a series of political slip-ups including the defeat in Congress of constitutional reforms aimed at curbing the military's power. His removal had long been rumoured.

The most surprising change was in education, in which Sergio Molina was replaced by Budget Chief Jose Pablo Arellano, who only an hour before the reshuffle had held a news conference to announce the government's 1997 budget.

Arellano is a well-known economist. Like all the appointees, he is considerably younger than the person he is replacing, reinforcing reports in local media that Frei sought a fresher image for his government.

Agriculture Minister Emiliano Ortega was replaced by chief trade negotiator Carlos Mladinic, and Transport and Communications Minister Narciso Irureta was replaced by his number two, Transport Secretary Claudio Hohmann.
Planning Minister Luis Maira was replaced by Roberto Pizarro, currently Chile's ambassador in Ecuador.

Mladinic was best known as chief negotiator of Chile's recent free trade agreement with the four-nation Mercosur bloc. His naming as agriculture minister is likely to be seen as a blow to farmers who angrily opposed the Mercosur pact, charging it will flood Chile with cheap Argentine grain.
Mercosur, a customs union grouping Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay, was inaugurated in 1995.
The Cabinet reshuffle was the second in Frei's 30-month-old government, after a shakeup of key political ministers in late 1994.
